articles.title: BMW Q3 profit falls 15% as China competition weighs
articles.content: BMW reported a 15% year-on-year decline in third-quarter net profit to 1.45 billion euros, a day after issuing its second profit warning of 2026. Intensifying competition from Chinese automakers, rising costs and weaker demand in China are weighing on the German luxury carmaker. Its vehicle deliveries in China plunged 24.8% during the quarter, while global deliveries fell 6.3%.

articles.title: Silver prices jump over 4% to reclaim $51/oz as Democrats secure US midterm victory. What’s happening?
articles.content: Silver prices surged over 4% to reclaim the $51/oz mark after Democrats secured a victory in the US midterm elections, weakening the dollar and Treasury yields. However, HSBC expects further gains to be limited as silver trades close to levels justified by fundamentals. Industrial and jewellery demand may weaken, while institutional buying and supply constraints could offer support.

articles.title: Warren Buffett has lived through 16 US Presidents. Why he ignores election impact on markets
articles.content: Warren Buffett believes investors should not let political uncertainty or election outcomes dictate their market decisions. articles.title: Democrats’ win rattles Trump trades from AI stocks to crypto
articles.content: The recent Democratic majority in Congress triggered a downturn in global markets, most notably impacting technology stocks. Investors are now wary about President Trump’s policies and their implications for AI investments. Conversely, solar stocks saw an uptick, signaling potential changes to clean energy regulations. Additionally, Treasury yields dropped as heightened oversight dampens fiscal stimulus hopes, while cryptocurrencies also fell amid uncertainty surrounding upcoming industry regulations.

articles.title: Oil slide, Treasury strength boost Indian bonds
articles.content: Indian government bonds experienced an increase due to a significant decline in crude oil prices. A Democratic sweep in the US midterm elections raised hopes for peace in the Middle East. Traders responded positively, adding positions in government bonds as yields softened. Concerns about inflation risks diminished as investors anticipated a delay in interest rate hikes. Market dynamics indicate that Qatar-led mediation efforts are being monitored closely amid these developments.

articles.title: US bond yields fall; Nasdaq, Dow Jones futures slip 2% as Democrats set for big win in US midterm elections
articles.content: US Treasury yields fell on Tuesday as investors sought safe-haven assets amid a sharp sell-off in US equity futures following projections of significant Democratic gains in the 2026 midterm elections. The 10-year yield slipped nearly 5 bps to 4.902%, while the 2-year yield dropped 6 bps to 4.55%.

articles.title: Titan Company Q2 results preview: Profit may rise up to 27% YoY; jewellery growth, margins in focus

articles.title: Diwali 2026: Will Sensex, Nifty reclaim their peaks or scale new highs? Analysts map the road ahead
articles.content: Market analysts are tentatively optimistic about Indian equity markets seeing a resurgence in the next financial year.
